sources.outlet: Journal of Urgent Care Medicine (Alan A. Ayers), 'Rural Urgent Care Growth Continues, But Challenges Remain'
sources.searcher_note: Quote is a row of Figure 2 'Largest Rural Urgent Care Operators, 2024' (Fast Pace first, 269 centers). Same article discusses the 2021 CMS RHC rate change and says 'the RHC model presents a paradox' for urgent care. Does not count Fast Pace RHC enrollments or its share of new RHCs. HTML version (jucm.com/rural-urgent-care-growth-continues-but-challenges-remain/) shows the figure only as an image.

sources.outlet: Journal of Urgent Care Medicine (Alan A. Ayers)
sources.quote: Began as one clinic in the small town of Collinwood, TN (population 949) in the fall of 2009 and has since expanded to 95 locations in four states.
sources.searcher_note: Pre-2021 profile of Fast Pace as an all-rural urgent-care chain (95 clinics); no RHC mention. Useful only as baseline for growth. Site blocks curl; quote via WebFetch.

notes: No source found that counts Fast Pace's rural health clinic enrollments or its share of new for-profit RHCs after the Consolidated Appropriations Act 2021 RHC payment change. Coverage found: trade press on rural urgent-care growth naming Fast Pace as the largest rural urgent-care operator; company and PE (Revelstoke, Shore Capital) press releases on clinic counts (company pages now say 280+ centers); PESP Jan 2023 report lists Fast Pace in a table of PE-owned rural providers (200 locations) with no RHC finding. No OIG, DOJ or CMS action found. No coverage dated July-Sept 2026 found. A Fast Pace careers page says a partner clinic group's 'clinics are certified as Rural Health Clinics' but that text is about a partner, not Fast Pace's own count.
